obn_gran.text: I've watched every ferry come in since 1958. The first rule of Oban: don't stand where the ferry is about to go. The second is: bring a coat.
Gaelic's still spoken round here, you'll hear 'madainn mhath', that's good morning, and 'ciamar a tha thu', how are you. It's pronounced 'kimmer a ha oo', and nobody expects you to get it right.

then.text: Back for the Scotch Broth? Kitchen's yours.

else.text: Och, come in out of that wind. The broth's been on since breakfast.
Barley first, so it has time to swell. Then every root in the house goes in, chopped small. It sticks to your ribs, and that's the idea.
Pop in whenever you've got the makings. Use my kitchen.
